R392.note: Splits GET (safe confirmation form, self-contained) from POST (CrossOriginProtection-wrapped delete), matching the file's existing pattern; email-link convenience and legitimate delete both still work.

R393.note: CRLF check plus alphanumeric-only allowlist blocks the injection, but the allowlist also rejects legitimate report filenames containing spaces/parentheses etc. beyond what's needed to stop CRLF, without flagging that tradeoff.

R394.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet correctly closes RESP injection and preserves key/value semantics, but changes RedisWireWriter's constructor from TcpClient to IConnectionMultiplexer; write-up openly notes the DI/initialization call site (not in the shown files) must be updated too.

R395.note: SandboxedEnvironment is Jinja2's supported mechanism for untrusted templates; self-contained swap, preserves render/return contract for legitimate previews.

R396.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode at the sink correctly neutralizes the reflected value; no other observable change.

R397.note: Parameterized query via placeholder + args is the correct database/sql pattern, identical query semantics to the original.

R398.note: escapeshellarg alone would close the vector; the added hostname allowlist is stricter than needed and silently rejects valid IPv6 hosts by returning reachable:false rather than an error.

R399.note: GET->POST + [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the correct pattern, but the ConfirmDelete view's link (not shown/modified) will break until it's changed to a token-carrying POST form; write-up discloses this as out of scope.

R400.note: Regex rejects only control characters, closing the CRLF injection while leaving normal folder-name characters (spaces, letters, quotes) unaffected.

R401.note: Classic save-next-before-free fix; preserves order, single free, and continued traversal exactly per the stated contract.

R402.note: Standard RFC4515-style LDAP filter escaping applied before the search call; escaping the extra '/' character is harmless and legitimate cn values are unaffected.

R403.note: CGI::escapeHTML applied at both interpolation points closes the XSS with no other observable change.

R404.note: Absolute-path rejection plus Clean+prefix containment check (with separator) correctly closes traversal; legitimate in-tree file requests are unaffected.

R405.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword with a dummy-hash timing guard is the right mechanism, but it requires existing plaintext-stored passwords to be migrated to bcrypt hashes before any real user can log in again; disclosed in the explanation but not applied within the fix.

R406.note: Named parameter via setParameter() closes the HQL injection with identical LIKE-pattern semantics.

R407.note: Method-type check inside keyFunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods(["HS256"]) is the documented golang-jwt fix for algorithm confusion; legitimate HS256 tokens are unaffected.

R408.note: Switching to flask_wtf.FlaskForm is the right mechanism, but it only protects once the template renders {{ form.csrf_token() }}; that template file isn't shown/updated, though the write-up does call it out as required.
